title: Standing notice (notice/v1)
description: A rule between runtimes, broadcast to every registered runtime. The machine that decides whether a record holds is governance/notices/notice_records.py (validate_notice); this schema documents the same rules for a reader and for any other tool. `requires_ack` is a SELECTOR, never a list of runtime ids: the effective requirement is computed from the registry (governance/notices/runtime_registry.py) on every read, so a runtime registered later is covered by every standing notice already issued. A literal id list is refused by name (hand-maintained-ack-list). Records live under the fleet's runtime state (.fleet/notices/<id>/notice.json) and are never committed; the shipped half is this schema, the module and the gate.

schema.description: The record version. A record carrying any other value is refused by name.

id.description: The stable notice id, and the name of the directory holding it. A notice is immutable: a correction is a new id that supersedes this one.

subject.description: One line naming the rule, so an ack names what it acknowledged.

body.description: The rule itself, in the words the runtimes must act on.

issued.description: When the notice was issued, in UTC. A timestamp with no zone is refused: a rule whose age cannot be read cannot be re-checked.

issued_by.description: The seat that issued it (the director, by default).

status.description: standing = every registered runtime owes an ack; withdrawn = the rule is retired, so nothing is owed (the record stays, because a rule that was broadcast leaves a trace).

requires_ack.description: The one accepted value is the selector 'registered-runtimes'. Any literal runtime id is refused by name (hand-maintained-ack-list).

refs.description: Where the rule comes from (an issue, a PR, a decision record), so the notice is a pointer and not a second authority.
